findings.pdf_says: DIVIDE { identifier-1 / literal-1 } INTO { identifier-2 / literal-2 }   -- both operand groups are printed with true BRACES (curly '{' ... '}'), stacked over two lines. Same in Format 5: DIVIDE { identifier-2 / literal-2 } BY { identifier-1 / literal-1 }.
findings.markdown_says:
```
           ⌐ identifier-1 ¬        ⌐ identifier-2 ¬
DIVIDE     |              | INTO   |               |
           └ literal-1   ┘        └ literal-2    ┘
```  (identical corner-glyph delimiter used again in Format 5)
findings.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2/5.2.6.3 a BRACE means exactly one of the stacked alternatives SHALL be chosen, while a BRACKET means at most one (the whole group may be omitted). The markdown renders the PDF's braces with the corner glyphs ⌐ ¬ └ ┘, which in this very document's own convention are the BRACKET shape — Formats 1, 2 and 3 of the same DIVIDE statement (page 644) render braces as ⎧⎨⎩ / ⎫⎬⎭ and brackets as ⎡⎣ / ⎤⎦. Read as brackets, Formats 4 and 5 would falsely permit 'DIVIDE INTO ...' with the dividend/divisor operand omitted. Formats 4 and 5 are the only DIVIDE formats in the file left in the un-normalized OCR glyph set.
findings.suggested_repair:
Re-render Format 4 and Format 5 with the file's brace convention, e.g.
```
           ⎧ identifier-1 ⎫      ⎧ identifier-2 ⎫
DIVIDE     ⎨              ⎬ INTO ⎨              ⎬
           ⎩ literal-1    ⎭      ⎩ literal-2    ⎭
```
and the mirror form for Format 5 (identifier-2/literal-2 BY identifier-1/literal-1).

findings.pdf_says: [|  ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1  |]  /  [|  NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2  |]  — a bracket with a vertical CHOICE-INDICATOR bar just inside each side; DIVIDE, INTO, BY, GIVING, REMAINDER, ON, SIZE, ERROR, NOT and END-DIVIDE are all underlined (required words).
findings.markdown_says:
```
⌐⌐ ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1       ¬¬
⌊⌊ NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2   ┘┘
[ END-DIVIDE ]
```
(no '> **Figure notes ...**' paragraph follows either Format 4 or Format 5)
findings.why_it_matters: The choice indicators survive only as doubled corner glyphs, which read as two nested brackets rather than as 5.2.6.4 choice indicators, and — unlike DIVIDE Formats 1, 2 and 3 on page 644, each of which carries a 'Figure notes' paragraph stating '⚠ The ON SIZE ERROR group is enclosed in CHOICE INDICATORS' and listing the underlined required words — Formats 4 and 5 carry no Figure notes at all. So for Formats 4 and 5 the file records neither the 5.2.6.4 semantics (ON SIZE ERROR, NOT ON SIZE ERROR, BOTH, or neither, in any order) nor which words are required.
findings.suggested_repair: Normalize the SIZE ERROR group to the file's '⎡|  ... |⎤' / '⎣|  ... |⎦' form and append a Figure notes paragraph to Format 4 and Format 5 matching the Format 1–3 notes, naming DIVIDE, INTO/BY, GIVING, REMAINDER, ON, SIZE, ERROR, NOT, END-DIVIDE as the underlined required words.

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.11.4   General rules  (bold run-in heading, one level below '14.9.11 DISPLAY statement', at the same level as 14.9.11.1 General, 14.9.11.2 General formats and 14.9.11.3 Syntax rules)
findings.markdown_says: ## 14.9.11.4 General rules   (H2 — while its siblings on the preceding pages are '### 14.9.11.1 General', '### 14.9.11.2 General formats', '### 14.9.11.3 Syntax rules', and its parent is '## 14.9.11 DISPLAY statement')
findings.why_it_matters: At H2 the General rules subsection becomes a SIBLING of the statement it belongs to instead of a child, so the document outline/TOC detaches every DISPLAY general rule from the DISPLAY statement. The file's own convention elsewhere (e.g. 14.9.9.1-.4, 14.9.15.1-.4) is '## 14.9.N <statement>' with '### 14.9.N.M <subsection>'.
findings.suggested_repair: Change '## 14.9.11.4 General rules' to '### 14.9.11.4 General rules'.

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.12.4   General rules  (bold run-in heading, one level below '14.9.12 DIVIDE statement', same level as 14.9.12.3 Syntax rules)
findings.markdown_says: ## 14.9.12.4 General rules   (H2 — while the immediately preceding sibling on page 645 is '### 14.9.12.3 Syntax rules' and the parent is '## 14.9.12 DIVIDE statement')
findings.why_it_matters: Same defect as 14.9.11.4: the General rules block is promoted to sibling-of-the-statement level, breaking the outline and detaching the DIVIDE general rules from the DIVIDE statement. It is also internally inconsistent with 14.9.12.3 two pages earlier, which is correctly H3.
findings.suggested_repair: Change '## 14.9.12.4 General rules' to '### 14.9.12.4 General rules'.

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.13.4   General rules  (bold run-in heading, one level below '14.9.13 EVALUATE statement', same level as 14.9.13.1 General and 14.9.13.2 General format)
findings.markdown_says: ## 14.9.13.4 General rules   (H2 — while '### 14.9.13.1 General' and '### 14.9.13.2 General format' are H3 and the parent is '## 14.9.13 EVALUATE statement')
findings.why_it_matters: Same defect: the EVALUATE general rules become a sibling of the EVALUATE statement rather than a child, breaking the outline. (14.9.13.3 Syntax rules, on page 650, is H2 for the same reason.)
findings.suggested_repair: Change '## 14.9.13.4 General rules' to '### 14.9.13.4 General rules' (and likewise '## 14.9.13.3 Syntax rules' → '### ...').
